## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sukkadhamma Sutta* ("Bright Things", Iti 42, PTS It 36) is the fifteenth discourse in the second chapter (*Dukanipāta*) of the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral]. The discourse teaches that two bright qualities (*sukkā dhammā*)—namely conscience (*hiri*) and prudence or moral shame (*ottappa*)—serve as guardians that safeguard the world (*dve'me bhikkhave sukkā dhammā lokaṃ pālenti*) [SuttaCentral; de La Vallée Poussin 1903]. Without these two protective principles, moral order would disintegrate and human beings would fail to respect familial and social boundaries [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral records a full parallel in Chinese translation in the *Benshi jing* (T 765.87) and passage-level parallels in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 2.8) and the *Theragāthā* (Thag 18.1) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies 56 Pali-internal text-reuse matches across six texts, showing especially dense shared phrasing with the *Dukanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 2, §2.1–2.6 matching AN 2.8/9), which aligns with SuttaCentral's curated parallel [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects shared segments with the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā*, *Majjhimanikāya-aṭṭhakathā*, *Abhidhammāvatāra-purāṇaṭīkā*, and another *Itivuttaka* text (Iti 31, *Ātapanīya Sutta*), alongside cross-language alignments with the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) and *Ekottarikāgama* (T 125) [DharmaNexus].

In modern scholarship, the sutta's opening phrasing is cited by Louis de La Vallée Poussin in his annotated edition of Candrakīrti's *Prasannapadā* [de La Vallée Poussin 1903]. SuttaCentral records 17 translations of the discourse across 15 modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].
